data.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel
data.detailed_description:
Among the nations on the Zemurian continent, the mighty Erebonian Empire has been quick to outwardly stake its claim militarily; yet politically, ugly bouts of internal conflict between the upper class and commoners attempting to rise to power have been steadily intensifying day by day. The Noble and Reformist Factions have been none too kind to one another over the years, and tensions between the two only stand to worsen if compromises aren’t made in the very near future.

Rean Schwarzer, like any other citizen of the Imperial Nation, is no stranger to these rising conflicts: the class system has been deeply embedded into the hearts of every Erebonian since the days of old. As a seventeen-year-old student preparing for his new life at Thors Military Academy, however, he notices that his crimson uniform differs from the standard ones issued to his peers—typically green for commoners, and white for nobles.

Enter, Class VII of Thors Military Academy. For the first time in the prestigious academy’s history, rank means nothing and skill means everything. With nine hand-picked students of various backgrounds and abilities, Rean included, Class VII readies itself to dive deep into the political quagmire that threatens not only them, but the Empire as a whole.
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Taking place on the same continent as the fan favorite Trails in the Sky offshoot of Nihon Falcom’s storied The Legend of Heroes franchise, Trails of Cold Steel (Sen no Kiseki in Japanese) is the first in the series to tread Erebonian soil and explore the inner political conflicts of this oft-mentioned powerhouse nation in detail. Delve into the expansive lore that has become synonymous with the series, enjoy school life and bond with fellow students to earn new abilities in battle, take advantage of speedy, tactical turn-based combat with the newly-developed “ARCUS” system, and uncover dramatic events that stand to change everything these two opposing social classes stand for.

    KEY FEATURES
  • A World Rich in Depth for Veterans and Newcomers Alike
    The events of Trails of Cold Steel are expertly told so that longtime Trails veterans and casual RPG fans alike can equally enjoy its detailed, highly nuanced storyline.

  • New Link System Adds Depth to Combat
    Take advantage of the Combat Link System by bonding with your allies throughout the school year, netting you a variety of combat benefits including healing, guarding and more.

  • A Sleek Update to a Classic Growth Mechanic
    Trails of Cold Steel streamlines the classic “Orbment” magic system from previous titles with new “ARCUS” units, allowing for more ready access to abilities and quicker customization.

  • Experience the Game as Never Before
    50% more lines of English voice-overs have been added to the PC release, bringing a fresh experience to even those who have played it before on console.

data.short_description: At Thors Military Academy, Erebonia’s best learn everything from the art of war to liberal arts. First year Rean Schwarzer learns he’s been selected to join the controversial Class VII, and they’ll need to deal with more than just class warfare--they’ll need to safeguard their country from chaos.

reviews.review:
first thing I should add the context of how I was playing the game: after Chapter 4 of this game I actually started Trails to Azure keeping this as spoiler free as possible I did a rotation of chapters between this game and Azure and it was one of the best experiences of narrative connectivity I've ever experienced it was almost seamless.

okay lets talk about cold steel itself having experienced the PC ports of the original trails in the sky trilogy and the crossbell duology you can tell alot of the QoL additions like Turbomode a more improved version of the notebook and ways to get potentially get missables if you well missed it all started with this entry so I found it a bit jarring when turbomode actually skips battle animations which create these weird loadtimes so seeing the first iteration of turbo definitely felt clunky and while the game runs well however it did take me a decent chunk of time to adjust how characters move in this game. the game is split into two section s per chapter: "freedays" where you bond with party members do sidequests, and finish it off with dungeon crawling this is probably the most divisive part of the game as the bonding events do add extra flavour to the cast it really doesn't add too much other than changes in dialogue. you can tell this game was influenced by Persona 3 and Persona 4 Golden as the tartarus like dungeon is implemented here and there really isn't much going for it other than very basic dungeons and bosses. but here's the thing since this is the trails signature "introduction" game whenever they start a new arc this was an interesting way for you to kinda do a "everyday life" type of immersion to help you get introduced to the massive nation of erebonia how well was it done? it was fine it just didn't add as much as I wanted for world building.

the second half of the games chapters are "field exersions" which feel more like what you'd be used to in a trails game where you visit a town, do quests do some dungeons and have the most story development in the chapter, these are more interesting in the game and are generally the most engaging part of each chapter it there's nothing to complain about other than me wishing I could explore the fields out of these towns and cities more.

the overall story is interesting Rean has some interesting characterisation but you can tell he has alot of things that will develop over the arc so I hope it gets better with him as things go on but I think he's a good character to show us erebonia and looking for a purpose. and like previous arcs where we look at the world from different faction POVs with the bracer guild in sky, and the police force with crossbell, this time  we at it from the lens of the military and while it has a highschool setting it still has some interesting dynamics and plot twists due to the faction we are a part of but I think the biggest short coming this game has is the ambition of this arc as a whole. before the final chapter there was meant to be an intermission that was sadly scrapped but was made into a drama CD called "returning" and funnily enough it has some important character development (thankfully Xseed has made a translation of the dramas script so we can still; experience it) which is just one example where they aimed too close to the sun will all these huge ideas as this is also the first 3D Trails game as well. I have alot of respect for what they did for this game  but I definitely hope the later entries help feel more polished and consistent. but overall I enjoyed my time with this game, it deff leaned into the anime tropes more than previous games but I think because of its highschool setting it leaned into it more but if you're able to look past that I still think this is a great trails entry just has alot of minor issues that build up as you play.
